key_developments: DELTA vs morning: US-Iran agreed to a two-week ceasefire brokered by Pakistan; Friday Islamabad talks scheduled; Brent settled at $94.75 (up $0.31 from $94.44 morning) and WTI at $94.41 (down $0.57 from $94.98 morning) on relief that Hormuz could reopen, though physical traffic remains below 10% of normal.

Israel conducted its heaviest Lebanon strikes since the conflict escalated, publicly stating Lebanon is excluded from the ceasefire; Iranian parliamentary speaker said three key ceasefire clauses were violated within hours of announcement, creating immediate credibility gap.

Hormuz remains permit-based and effectively restricted: shippers lack clarity on transit terms, Iran Sepah navy warned unapproved vessels will be targeted, and normalization timelines are measured in weeks not hours — Qatar LNG and helium supply chain risk persists.
